successors.note: 788: 'The last tribal stem duchy to be incorporated was Bavaria in 788.' Cliopatria's Frankish shape of 788 contains 487 of the 488 cells of the Bavarian shape of 787.

capitals.name: Regensburg (Ratisbona)
capitals.note: 'Theodo established his capital at Ratisbona'; the Agilolfings page: 'Their Bavarian residence was at Regensburg'. No page dates the residence before Theodo (680-716), so the span back to 540 is the researcher's reading. After the partition before 715 Theodbert reigned at Salzburg (from 702), Tassilo II at Passau and Grimoald at Freising (c. 716-725).

keyframe_review.note: 76,734 km2: Bavaria with Alpine Tyrol and the Salzburg lowlands. The Bavarians page gives no area; its footnote gives 70,549 km2 for modern Bavaria (ratio 1.09). Pre-ducal: History of Bavaria says the name 'existed by about 520 AD' and the Duchy page dates the duchy to 'c. 551/555'; the shape is kept as the people's land and the state's story begins in the ledger at 540 (Cliopatria's start).

81,235 km2: the shape takes an Alpine strip of 14 cells (12.9-13.7E, 46.5-47.0N, about 3,500 km2) that lay inside Cliopatria's Ostrogothic shape of 550. The Duchy page dates the first documented duke Garibald I to 'c. 555' ('ruled from 555 onward as a largely independent Merovingian vassal'); it does not mention the Alpine strip (unverified: page silent).

Same outline as 567-591. Tassilo I is named rex in 591 (Garibald I page) and the dynasty continues; no border change.
Same outline. The pages opened give no territorial event for 602-611 (the Battle of Aguntum, about 610, would not load: pages_failed in the report).

Same outline to 632. Unverified: page silent on any change between 612 and 632.

73,644 km2: the shape loses 30 cells (about 7,600 km2, 12.2-14.6E, 46.5-49.1N) along the eastern and south-eastern edge, 27 of them inside Cliopatria's Samo's Empire shape of 640. The Samo page dates his realm 631-658 and his victory over Dagobert I 'in 631 or 632' but says nothing of Bavaria, so the loss is Cliopatria's and unverified; kept as drawn, event at confidence 1.

The other 18 lost cells of 633 stay outside and become Cliopatria's Carantania from 661 (Carantania page: 'a smaller part of the March came to be known as Carantania'). Unverified for Bavaria.

Outline unchanged (39 vertices). Theodo 'divided his duchy' among his sons 'sometime before 715' (Theodbert at Salzburg from 702, Tassilo II at Passau, Grimoald at Freising); the partition is internal, the duchy stays one for the map.
Outline unchanged. Grimoald, duke at Freising c. 716-725, later ruled all of Bavaria (Agilolfings page); internal.
Outline unchanged. Hugbert duke 725-737 (Agilolfings page); no territorial event on the pages.

Outline unchanged (76,428 km2). Odilo duke from 737 and married Charles Martel's daughter Hiltrud in 741 (Odilo page). Carantania, drawn as its own Cliopatria shape 741-749, is vassalised about 743 (ledger).

122,313 km2 against 76,428 km2 for 741-749: the +45,016 km2 is exactly Cliopatria's Carantania shape of 749 (the shape minus Carantania 749 equals the 661 shape to one cell). The pages opened say Carantania was a vassal principality under Bavarian and Frankish overlordship, not incorporated (none of the pages opened says it was), so it is drawn as a vassal of Bavaria in the lighter tint from the ledger's 743 vassal_start. No infobox area on the Bavarians or Duchy page to compare.

correction.text: The Bavarian duchy proper: Cliopatria's shape without the Carantanian shape of 749 that it absorbs from 750. The duke 'vassalised the Slavic princes of Carantania' about 743 and Carantania accepted 'the overlordship of Bavaria and the Frankish kingdom'; it is a vassal (lighter tint), not direct land. The eastern border is the Enns ('the eastern Bavarian border, towards the Avars, was situated on the river Enns').

ledger.note: 540: the Bavarii, first named 'by about 520', appear as a people on the Danube and the northern Alps (Cliopatria's start); the duchy proper begins about 555. Page silent on 540: the year is Cliopatria's; the Bavarians page says only 'first mentioned in the mid-6th century'.

ledger.note: 546: a few edge cells are added to the Bavarian shape (Cliopatria). Page silent; two of the five cells lie in the Lombard shape of 545, one in the Ostrogothic.

c. 555: Garibald I, first documented duke, rules the Bavarians as an Agilolfing duke under Merovingian overlordship. 'ruled from 555 onward as a largely independent Merovingian vassal'; infobox 'c. 555-788'; the Agilolfings page lists him from 548, the Garibald page 'from 555 until 591'.

ledger.note: 555: the Alpine edge is added to the shape (Cliopatria; 14 of its 15 cells lay in the Ostrogothic shape of 550). Page silent on the land; the date is Cliopatria's and coincides with the first duke.

ledger.note: 633: Samo's Slavic union takes the eastern fringe of Bavaria (Cliopatria; 27 of the 30 cells lie in its 640 shape). The Samo page dates the union to 631-658 and 'Lower Austria' to its lands but does not mention Bavaria: bridging judgement.

region.text: the north-eastern part of the lost strip, about 3,000 km2 (Upper Austria and the Bohemian Forest edge)

ledger.note: 661: part of the fringe returns to Bavaria after Samo's union ends ('Samo's death in 658 or 659'); the rest becomes Carantania. Page silent on Bavaria: the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the Slavic principality of Carantania in modern Carinthia, parts of Styria, East Tyrol and Salzburg

ledger.note: c. 743: Duke Odilo makes the Slavic princes of Carantania his vassals. 'At around 743, the Bavarian duke Odilo vassalised the Slavic princes of Carantania'; the Carantania page has Boruth ask Odilo for help against the Avars 'about 740' and lists the principality as a 'tributary to Franks: 745', so the Franks share the overlordship.

region.text: Carantania, whose Bavarian overlord is deposed

ledger.note: 788: with the duchy absorbed by the Franks, the Bavarian overlordship of Carantania ends and the Frankish one remains (integration into the Frankish realm follows in 828). The page does not date the end of the Bavarian overlordship; bridging judgement.

region.text: the whole duchy, Altbayern and its eastern march to the Enns

ledger.note: 788: Charlemagne deposes Tassilo III and Bavaria is absorbed into the Frankish kingdom. 'The last tribal stem duchy to be incorporated was Bavaria in 788'; Tassilo 'was deposed during a diet in the Imperial Palace Ingelheim in 788' (Tassilo III page) and renounced his claims at Frankfurt in 794.

wars.name: Frankish-Bavarian war of 743
wars.outcome: Odilo, who 'rebelled to support the Alamans with the support of Hunald I of Aquitaine in 742/43', was 'defeated in 743 after a battle at the river Lech' and 'had to accept Frankish overlordship over Bavaria, but remained duke'.
wars.note: No border moved; the Frankish suzerainty over Bavaria is for the kingdom-of-the-franks dossier (vassal_start, counterpart bavarians). Charles Martel's earlier campaigns into Bavaria are not on the pages opened.

wars.name: Odilo's intervention in Carantania
wars.outcome: Odilo 'came to the aid of Prince Boruth of Carantania against repeated Avar incursions' and 'was able to vassalize the Slavic principality in the southeast'.
wars.note: The Carantania page dates Boruth's request 'about 740'; the Duchy page dates the vassalisation 'around 743'.

wars.name: Avar incursion into Bavaria of 788
wars.outcome: 'Already in 788, the Avars made an incursion into Bavaria', where 'the Avars suffered a significant defeat (788)'; the eastern Bavarian border towards the Avars then lay on the Enns.
wars.note: The first act of the Frankish-Avar wars, which began from Bavarian soil: 'Bavaria then became the main base for the Frankish campaign against the Avars, which was initiated in 791.' No border moved.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on the pages opened. The one named frontier is the Enns towards the Avars about 788 ('the eastern Bavarian border, towards the Avars, was situated on the river Enns'), still an approximate river line; the southern Alpine edge and the Thuringian and Slavic fringes are soft.

notes:
Bavarians, 540-788 (19 Cliopatria shapes, 9 pages + the Samo page opened for the Avar dossier).
- Cliopatria begins in 540; the pages date the people 'by about 520', the duchy 'c. 551/555'. The state starts in 540 at confidence 1 and a rename event at 555 carries the first duke.
- The 750-787 shapes absorb the Carantania shape of 749 (verified: shape minus Carantania 749 = the 661 shape to one cell). The pages say Carantania was a vassal under Bavarian then Frankish overlordship, so the verdict is adjust and a vassal_start (743) / vassal_end (788) pair carries it. The Carantania dossier (eu-06) should record its side of the relation (Bavarian then Frankish tributary from about 743/745) and not let Bavaria absorb it in 750.
- Frankish suzerainty over Bavaria (Merovingian from 555, 'strict dependence' under Charles Martel, 743 after the Lech, Pippin's ward Tassilo from 748/749, the oath at Compiegne 757) belongs in the kingdom-of-the-franks dossier (eu-07) as vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart 'bavarians'; the schema gives the vassal events to the suzerain. Pages: Duchy of Bavaria, Odilo, Tassilo III.
- The 546, 555, 633 and 661 border changes of Cliopatria are explained only from the shapes (neighbour intersections), not by the pages: confidence 1.
- The 630-680 gap in the Agilolfing list (no duke on the Agilolfings page) and the double-dating of Garibald I (548 or 555) are flagged in the rulers' notes.
- Pages that would not load: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Aguntum (about 610, Bavarians against the Slavs) - the article title may not exist; a gap-filler should try 'Agilolfings' sources or 'Tassilo I'.
- Not verified (page budget): Charles Martel's campaigns of 725 and 728, the Lombard border in the Adige valley (Trentino/Bolzano), the Bavarian marches in the Pustertal, the colonisation of the east after 788.
- Gazetteer: all names used exist (the shapes are cited as Cliopatria shapes).
